documents.population: International degree students, bachelor's applicants (2027/2028 September entry)
documents.notes: NTU Admission Guidelines for International Degree Students, '2027/2028 September Entry' (first round 29 September - 5 November 2026; second round 1 December 2026 - 19 January 2027). Departments may require further documents ('Available Degree Programs >> 2027 September entry'); the CSIE department's own list was not read. Not drafted (no vocabulary kind): Declaration and Authorization Form (system-generated, signed), payment receipt of the application fee, proof of Chinese proficiency (CEFR A2+) for Chinese-taught programmes, certificate of expected graduation/enrollment in place of the graduation certificate for current-year graduates, and the verification of credentials by an ROC overseas office for admitted applicants (a consular verification, not an apostille).

items.quote: Fill in the online application form
Bachelor's degree applicants: High school (or above) graduation certificate, or documents of equivalent educational level
Full transcript of records (including explanation of grading system)
may have the credentials translated on the condition that said translations are notarized by a ROC overseas representative office or by a registered translation agency
items.condition: the school does not issue the academic credentials in Chinese or English

items.quote: Applicants shall submit proof of English proficiency equivalent to CEFR B2 (Vantage) or above
items.condition: programme conducted in English (applicants from English-speaking countries may be exempt; an English-medium previous degree may replace the certificate)

items.quote: Recommendation Letters: to be written in Chinese or English by applicants' professors or employers.
items.condition: the department requires them ('Recommendation letters online (according to the department requirement)')

items.quote: Photograph: a close -up color shot of the head and shoulders (no hats) within the last 6 months.
Financial statement: Applicants are required to prove that they can finance their education and living expenses for studying in Taiwan.
